sources.name: One Skill to Rule Them All

skills.name: brainstorming
skills.description: You MUST use this before any creative work — creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.
headings: Anti-Pattern: Too Simple To Need Approval
skills.bodyExcerpt:
Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by classifying how much process the request needs, then work through your path: understand the context, refine the idea, present a design, and get your human partner's approval.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes.
skills.bodyExcerpt: A bug is a hypothesis about the system that has not been tested yet. Write the hypothesis down before changing anything.

skills.name: writing-plans
skills.description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code.
skills.bodyExcerpt: Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste.

skills.name: task-observer
skills.description: Monitors task execution for skill improvement opportunities. Captures patterns, user corrections, workflow insights, and methodology worth preserving as reusable skills.
skills.bodyExcerpt: Skills improve best from friction noticed during real work, not from sitting down to "improve a skill." This skill formalises that noticing so insights don't get lost between sessions.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance.
skills.bodyExcerpt: Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill.
